text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Clerides suggested procedure for opening mass graves in search for missing persons during meeting on Monday with Turkish Cypriot leader Denktash.
- Russian detained on suspicion of hacking into bank computer via Internet and running up big bills on other people's credit cards.
- Pavlos Georgiou found guilty of giving virus that causes AIDS to his British lover, Janette Pink.
- Elderly Cypriot "tried to rape British woman" in Paphos.
- Denktash does not want to attend second round of U.N. talks scheduled to take place in Geneva.
- Denktash studying Clerides proposals for opening graves of suspected missing persons.

- Trade unions in semi-governmental electricity authority say they do not want reinstatement of former board of directors. Board members were suspended last year amid allegations of irregularities in tender procedures; Supreme Court recently declared suspension null and void.
- Authorities consider plan to encourage winter tourism in Cyprus.
